changelog.old_reference_answer: The Student Handbook contains two different numeric thresholds. The undergraduate Absence section says a student accumulating unexcused absences equivalent to twenty percent (25%) of the total number of hours per day session for a particular subject shall be dropped from that subject, and time lost due to late enrolment counts as absence. The Dropping section says students shall be dropped if they have an accumulated absence of at least 25% of the total number of class hours in a semester. The graduate Attendance policy says absences equivalent to twenty percent (20%) of the total number of hour per day session for a particular subject shall cause the student to be dropped. The corpus therefore does not present a single consistent percentage for all students.
changelog.new_reference_answer: The Student Handbook does not state one absence-drop threshold that applies to every student. The undergraduate Attendance / Absence section says a student accumulating unexcused absences equivalent to twenty percent (25%) of the total number of hours per day session for a particular subject shall be dropped from that subject or class. That sentence writes the words twenty percent next to (25%). Time lost due to late enrolment is treated as absence. The undergraduate Dropping section says students shall be dropped if they have an accumulated absence of at least 25% of the total number of class hours in a semester. That is a semester class-hours measure, not the same wording as the per-day-session Absence section. The graduate Attendance policy says a student accumulating absences equivalent to twenty percent (20%) of the total number of hour per day session for a particular subject shall be dropped from that subject or class. That rule is in the Graduate Studies attendance article. These passages are different sections and, for the graduate card, a different student population. The corpus does not say which statement supersedes another.
